newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Draft accord reached in South African sugar strike.
newsitem.headline: Draft accord reached in South African sugar strike.

text.p: Management and unions reached a draft agreement in the early hours of Wednesday morning to settle a two-week strike which has crippled the South African sugar industry, a spokesman for the companies said.
The unions will now take the package back to their members, and management and unions will meet again on Thursday morning when the accord will hopefully be finalised, he told Reuters.
Some 4,000 Workers at 14 mills and refineries, operated by Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd TNTJ.J in the KwaZulu-Natal sugarcane belt, have been on strike over wages since July 2.

The sugar industry has estimated that it was losing some 83,500 tonnes of cane in production but officials said the blow has been softened somewhat by the early warning of impending strike action by the unions.
An industry source said the unions gave notice six days before the strike of their intention to strike.
Millers were able to notify sugar growers not to deliver cane to the mills, the source said, adding that cane on the fields would only lose some sucrose content.
He said the loss in production could be made up by extending the crushing season -- which usually runs from the beginning of April to just after Christmas.
No details of the draft agreement were made available.
